A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NPPC benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices G–L report original evaluations of ten LLMs on twelve NPC tasks, including performance, token usage, and failure analyses.

after.justification: The original evaluations remain, supplemented by benchmark-score correlations in Appendix A.9 and a reported QwQ-32B token-budget experiment in Appendix M.

M1.justification: The npgym, npsolver, and npeval procedures remain unchanged. In particular, the relaxed JSON parsing described in v2 already appears in v1's Appendix D code; the expanded discussion does not establish a new parser or method.

E1.justification: The 25-problem suite and twelve directly evaluated NPC tasks remain unchanged. Appendix A.9 adds model-score data from MMLU, GPQA Diamond, and LMArena for correlation analysis, extending the data used for validation without documenting new model runs on those tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark experiments retain the same ten models, as confirmed by v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 8. Newer models mentioned in v2 Appendix A.7 are proposed for future evaluation, not added comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix M adds a QwQ-32B diagnostic using a 32,768-token limit alongside the original 7,500-token setting. Appendix A.9 introduces correlation-based validation. The main experiments retain their difficulty configurations, one-shot prompts, and published hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Appendix A.9 adds an external-validity analysis relating NPPC scores to three established benchmarks. Appendix M extends the existing QwQ failure analysis with token-limit sensitivity, a token-limit frequency measurement, and a best-effort guessing example. Existing token, aha-moment, and other failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new correlation analysis reports Pearson and Spearman coefficients, p-values, and a significance threshold. The original three seeds, thirty instances per seed, and stratified bootstrap confidence-interval reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All twelve detailed benchmark tables retain identical scores and confidence intervals. New results include Pearson correlations of 0.798 with GPQA Diamond and 0.821 with LMArena, versus a nonsignificant 0.553 with MMLU. Appendix M newly reports 64.53% token-limit saturation for QwQ-32B and qualitatively reports no significant improvement with 32,768 tokens.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit reduction-based definition of NP-hardness and distinguishes it from NP-completeness. The existing NP definition, problem formulations, and mathematical content remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow 'uncrushable' to 'not crushed by current models' and replace the AGI-testbed framing with evaluating reasoning limits. The framework and principal performance claims remain. This qualification is incomplete because the conclusion still claims an 'uncrushable nature.'

C2.justification: Beyond relocating future-work discussion, v2 substantially expands interpretations of difficulty calibration, tool-use applicability, and QwQ failures. It adds specific multimodal obstacles, synthetic-task overfitting risks, and warnings against interpreting NPPC scores as general intelligence or real-world reliability, together with interpretations of the new correlations.

D1.justification: Appendices A.6 and A.8 provide additional calibration details and explicitly document leaderboard access; Appendix M specifies the larger diagnostic token budget. The code URL, model identifiers, parser implementation, and main hyperparameter table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The discussion substantially broadens positioning around live benchmarks, contamination, and NPC-based reinforcement learning. Added works include LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench-Live, NP-Engine, SATURN, SynLogic, and RLVE. These extend the research context beyond bibliographic updates to retained citations.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, difficulty explanations are expanded, and takeaway boxes organize the results. Costs move into the main text, future work becomes a main limitations section, and the QwQ discussion becomes a separate appendix.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the desiderata graphic and combines several diagrams into a detailed workflow overview. It adds leaderboard and correlation displays, redisplays the prompt template, and substantially reformats tables and page layout. The shortened main token figure and omitted main aha figure retain their complete counterparts in the appendices.

improvement.justification: The new correlation study, QwQ diagnostic, clearer workflow, and explicit overfitting and interpretation limitations improve support and readability around the unchanged core experiments. The gains remain limited: the larger-token experiment lacks numerical success rates and detailed run information, while the conclusion retains the overly broad 'uncrushable' claim despite qualifications elsewhere.
